title_en: Guangdong Provincial Light Industrial Products Import and Export Group Corporation v. TMT Trading Co., Ltd. — trademark ownership dispute appeal
keywords_en: Civil; trademark ownership dispute; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Guangdong Province; Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; legal person; Trademark Law; trademark ownership; attribution of trademark in OEM processing; relationship between trademark registrant and actual user; reversal of judgment; trademark registration; OEM processing; exclusive sales agreement; trademark license; good faith; trademark rights; trademark ownership dispute of a trading company
full_text_en:
Guangdong Province Light Industrial Products Import and Export Group Corporation
v.
TMT Trading Limited
— Dispute over Trademark Ownership (Appeal)

Promulgated by the Supreme People's Court No. 25 (2000)

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China
(1998) Zhi Zhong Zi No. 8

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Guangdong Province Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Corporation, domiciled at No. 2 Dezheng South Road, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.
Legal Representative: Liu Fashu, General Manager of the Corporation.
Agent ad litem: Guo Jinkai, lawyer of Guangdong Mingda Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Zhong Guocai, lawyer of Guangzhou Zhonglian Law Firm.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): TMT Trading Limited, domiciled at Room 11-14, 12/F, Block B, Hong Kong Industrial Centre, 489-491 Castle Peak Road, Kowloon, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.
Legal Representative: Wang Shaoming, Chairman of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Li Jingbing, lawyer of Beijing Zhengjian Yongshen Law Firm.

The appellant, Guangdong Province Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Corporation (hereinafter referred to as "Light Industrial Products Company"), appealed to this Court against the civil judgment (1998) Yue Fa Zhi Chu Zi No. 2 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court in the dispute over trademark ownership with the appellee, TMT Trading Limited (hereinafter referred to as "TMT Company"). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing of this case. The appellant's agents ad litem, Guo Jinkai and Dong Yidong (original agent ad litem, later replaced by Zhong Guocai), and the appellee's legal representative, Wang Shaoming, and agent ad litem, Li Jingbing, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The trial of this case has now concluded.

The judgment of the first instance found: For the purpose of developing new products, Light Industrial Products Company, during the Spring 1979 Chinese Export Commodities Fair, negotiated with Wang Shaoming, General Manager of Hong Kong Dongming Trading Limited (hereinafter referred to as "Dongming Company"), and others regarding the production and export of ceiling fans, and unanimously agreed to use the "TMT" trademark provided by Dongming Company, and that no other foreign merchants should order TMT-branded ceiling fans from Light Industrial Products Company. On September 15, 1979, and November 1, 1980, Dongming Company and Light Industrial Products Company respectively signed two "Exclusive Sales Agreements," stipulating that Dongming Company would manufacture under its own brand and exclusively sell TMT and TMC brand ceiling fans, and would provide free of charge the enameled wire, bearings, capacitors, UL lead wires, trademarks, etc., necessary for producing the ceiling fans, and that Light Industrial Products Company would arrange production. It was also agreed that Dongming Company would invest in and adopt various effective methods for advertising promotion, and the patterns and text used should be agreed upon in advance with Light Industrial Products Company. On June 20, 1981, Dongming Company published a statement in Hong Kong's "Sing Tao Daily": "Our company has been honored by Light Industrial Products Company as the exclusive distributor of TMT brand ceiling fans since January 1, 1980." On February 24, 1981, Light Industrial Products Company and Dongming Company jointly published a statement in the "People's Daily" declaring Dongming Company as the exclusive general distributor of TMT brand ceiling fans. The two agreements concerning the ownership of the "TMT," "TMC, SMC, SMT" trademarks, signed between Light Industrial Products Company and Dongming Company on July 11, 1980, and January 23, 1981, provided by Light Industrial Products Company, stipulated that the ownership of the said trademarks belonged to Light Industrial Products Company, and entrusted Mr. Wang Shaoming with full authority to represent Light Industrial Products Company in applying for registration of the "TMT, TMC, SMT, SMC" brand household electrical appliance products in Hong Kong and all major electrical appliance sales regions worldwide. However, neither of these two agreements bore the seal of the company, and TMT Company claimed that they were invalid. Light Industrial Products Company registered the TMT trademark with the State Administration for Industry and Commerce in 1980. To prevent other companies from imitating or passing off the TMT trademark, Light Industrial Products Company also registered the TMC and SMT trademarks in 1981. TMT Company registered the TMT trademark in Hong Kong and some Middle Eastern countries. In March 1982, Dongming Company ceased operations due to discord among its shareholders. Wang Shaoming, former General Manager of Dongming Company, and another shareholder, Lin Guiquan, established TMT Company, which took over the business of manufacturing ceiling fans under the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks previously conducted by Dongming Company and Light Industrial Products Company, and assumed responsibility for repaying the debts owed by Dongming Company to Light Industrial Products Company, and also succeeded to the three trademarks. After the establishment of TMT Company, in the multiple exclusive sales agreements and purchase confirmation letters signed with Light Industrial Products Company over the years (including agreements dated September 15, 1979; November 1, 1980; November 21, 1981; January 5, 1983; November 3, 1984; January 13, 1986; and confirmation letters dated November 27, 1979; December 8, 1980; and many subsequent confirmation letters), it was clearly stated that TMT Company provided the trademarks in dispute in this case. The authenticity of these agreements and confirmation letters was acknowledged and recognized by both parties. Over the years, TMT Company registered the TMT, SMT, and TMC trademarks in the main countries and regions where TMT brand ceiling fans are sold, and spent substantial sums on extensive advertising and promotion to market the said branded products, achieving a certain level of recognition for TMT brand products overseas, which also attracted many manufacturers to counterfeit TMT brand products. In 1983, TMT Company and Light Industrial Products Company jointly filed a lawsuit against Hong Kong Unitali Trading Limited for trademark infringement, and the Hong Kong High Court rendered a judgment on October 11, 1990, in favor of the two plaintiffs. On October 23 and December 16, 1987, Light Industrial Products Company issued two certification documents, certifying that the "TMT" trademark registered by Light Industrial Products Company under No. 142201 in 1980, and the "SMT" trademark under No. 151390 and "TMC" trademark under No. 151392 registered in 1981, were owned and beneficially held by TMT Company in Hong Kong, and that Light Industrial Products Company merely held these trademarks as a trustee on behalf of TMT Company. After seeing these two documents, Light Industrial Products Company suspected they might be forgeries and applied on May 20, 1998, for a judicial appraisal of the two documents concerning trademark ownership submitted by TMT Company.

The judgment of the first instance also found: On October 6, 1994, Light Industrial Products Company and TMT Company signed an agreement, stipulating: 1. Within China, the "TMT" brand trademark is registered by Light Industrial Products Company, which has absolute rights to operate and manage it. If any domestic company or manufacturer is found to counterfeit or infringe the "TMT" brand trademark, Light Industrial Products Company shall effectively stop such infringement or resolve it through legal channels, and the related costs within China shall be borne by Light Industrial Products Company. 2. Outside China (including Hong Kong), the "TMT" brand trademark is registered by TMT Company, which has absolute rights to operate and manage it. If any company or manufacturer is found to counterfeit or infringe the "TMT" brand trademark, TMT Company shall effectively stop such infringement or resolve it through legal channels, and the related costs shall be borne by TMT Company. 3. All "TMT" brand electric fans and their accessory products produced by TMT Company in China for export must be exported exclusively through Light Industrial Products Company. If, for any other reason, Light Industrial Products Company cannot provide export services, TMT Company may, with the consent of Light Industrial Products Company, arrange for export services through other companies or factories, but shall pay a trademark usage fee at 2% of the ex-factory price and sign a trademark usage agreement. After the execution of this agreement, conflicts arose between the parties during its performance. TMT Company claimed that Light Industrial Products Company failed to crack down on domestic manufacturers' infringement as agreed, causing substantial economic losses, and requested the return of the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks or their transfer to TMT Company for a sum of HKD 300,000 for the change of name procedures. Light Industrial Products Company argued that TMT Company failed to pay the trademark usage fee as agreed, with an outstanding amount of USD 19,232, and had arranged for production and sales within China without authorization. Over the years, the parties engaged in negotiations to resolve the trademark dispute but failed to reach a consensus. Light Industrial Products Company then filed a record of intellectual property protection with the General Administration of Customs. As a result, products manufactured by TMT Company in China could not be exported, causing inventory backlogs for the manufacturers.

The judgment of the first instance further found: He Yaosong and Wu E, former handlers of Light Industrial Products Company, submitted a written report to the company's leadership on December 25, 1997, concerning the TMT trademark issue, stating: In early 1980, Wang Shaoming, General Manager of Dongming Company, brought the TMT trademark, which he had designed himself, to the company, requesting its use on exported ceiling fans. According to Wang Shaoming, the trademark was derived from the first three letters of the English name of Dongming Company, TUNG MING TRADING CO., LTD. After discussions with the company's leadership, it was agreed to use this trademark. After using the trademark, Wang Shaoming proposed trademark registration in 1980. However, as the national trademark law had not yet been promulgated, foreign merchants were not allowed to register trademarks domestically. After discussions, it was decided that the domestic registration of the trademark would be handled by Light Industrial Products Company, while overseas registration would be handled by Dongming Company. Subsequently, following Wang Shaoming's suggestion, the registration of the TMC and SMT trademarks was also processed. Before 1985, all TMT trademarks used on TMT brand ceiling fans were printed by Dongming Company in Hong Kong and provided free of charge to Light Industrial Products Company for use in production. The designated manufacturers of TMT brand ceiling fans, namely Guizhou No.1 Fan Factory, Sanshui County Local State-owned Electromechanical Factory, and Zhongshan Household Electrical Appliances General Factory, all confirmed that TMT Company continuously provided market information and technical support to the manufacturers and regularly sent personnel to inspect product quality.

The original name of Light Industrial Products Company was China Light Industrial Products Import and Export Corporation, Guangdong Branch. On October 7, 1987, with the approval of the Guangdong Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce, the company name was changed to: China Light Industrial Products Import and Export Corporation, Guangdong (Group) Company (first name), and China Light Industrial Products Import and Export Corporation, Guangdong Branch (second name). On February 24, 1989, with the approval of the Guangdong Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce, the company name was changed to: Guangdong Province Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Corporation.

TMT Company filed a lawsuit with the Guangdong High People's Court on the grounds that Light Industrial Products Company had violated the two parties' entrustment arrangements, intending to appropriate the trademarks that TMT Company had entrusted it to register in China, and had prevented the export of TMT Company's branded processing products, causing economic losses. It requested the court to: terminate the relationship under which Light Industrial Products Company was entrusted to register and manage the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks in China; order Light Industrial Products Company to return the property obtained through the entrustment relationship and compensate for losses of RMB 100 million; order Light Industrial Products Company to bear the litigation costs and TMT Company's attorney's fees; and impose penalties on Light Industrial Products Company in accordance with the law.

After trial, the Guangdong High People's Court held that the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks in dispute were originally designed and first and actually used by Dongming Company. Subsequently, through mutual agreement, these trademarks were temporarily registered and managed in China by Light Industrial Products Company. After Dongming Company was dissolved, TMT Company, established by its shareholders Wang Shaoming and Lin Guiquan, took over the business of operating ceiling fans and other goods under the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks with Light Industrial Products Company, and also assumed the obligation to repay Dongming Company's debts. The above trademarks were also succeeded to by TMT Company. TMT Company's claim that it entrusted Light Industrial Products Company to register the trademarks in China is sufficiently supported by: the contracts and exclusive sales agreements signed since 1979; the written explanations of He Yaosong and Wu E, former handlers of Light Industrial Products Company, regarding the TMT trademark issue; the long-term cooperation between TMT Company and Light Industrial Products Company in branded production; and the two certification documents issued by Light Industrial Products Company in 1987. Although the expressions regarding ownership in the correspondence exchanged between the parties are somewhat inconsistent, this does not affect the reliability of this finding. Therefore, TMT Company's claim of ownership over these three trademarks also has a lawful basis. Based on the above reasoning, and considering that the three trademarks have consistently been used by TMT Company and its predecessor Dongming Company for branded production in mainland China, and that returning these trademarks to TMT Company would be conducive to continuing to play their proper role; that only TMT Company can lawfully distribute the three branded goods in overseas markets; and that conflicts have arisen between the parties, resulting in the loss of a basis for cooperation, with the situation and contradiction that the plaintiff cannot continue to organize production and export in mainland China while the defendant cannot sell the same brand products in relevant overseas regions, TMT Company's claim to terminate the entrustment relationship with Light Industrial Products Company and for the return of the above trademarks should be supported. Given that Light Industrial Products Company registered and effectively managed the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks in China, TMT Company should provide appropriate economic compensation when the trademarks are returned. Light Industrial Products Company suspected that the two certification documents concerning trademark ownership submitted by TMT Company to the court were forgeries and requested a judicial appraisal. However, due to Light Industrial Products Company's frequent changes of company seals in foreign economic activities, most of which were not filed, the comparison samples provided were difficult to accept, and Light Industrial Products Company was unable to provide sufficient evidence. Moreover, these two documents were not the sole evidence in this case, so Light Industrial Products Company's application was not adopted. Light Industrial Products Company argued that trademark ownership disputes should be under the jurisdiction of the trademark administrative authority and that the People's Court lacked jurisdiction over this case, requesting dismissal of the plaintiff's lawsuit. In response, according to the provisions of China's Trademark Law, the court only lacks jurisdiction over ownership disputes arising from improper registration. Since this case involves a dispute arising from entrustment registration, the People's Court has jurisdiction. Light Industrial Products Company's request lacks legal basis and is not adopted. Accordingly, the court of first instance, pursuant to Articles 4, 5, Paragraph 1 of Article 65, and Item (2) of Article 69 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 128 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered the following judgment: 1. Confirmed that the exclusive rights to the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks registered by Light Industrial Products Company belong to TMT Company. 2. TMT Company shall, after this judgment takes legal effect, handle the procedures for changing the ownership of the TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks with the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce of the People's Republic of China. 3. TMT Company shall, within one month from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Light Industrial Products Company in the amount of RMB 500,000. 4. Dismissed TMT Company's other claims. The litigation costs of RMB 510,010 were to be borne equally by TMT Company (RMB 255,005) and Light Industrial Products Company (RMB 255,005).

Light Industrial Products Company, dissatisfied with the above judgment of the Guangdong High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: The judgment of the first instance contained erroneous findings of fact. The appellant acquired exclusive rights to the disputed trademarks through registration. Neither the appellee nor Dongming Company ever registered the disputed trademarks with the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, nor is there any written entrustment document proving that the appellant was entrusted to register the said trademarks. The agreement signed by the parties on October 6, 1994, once again clearly stipulated that the ownership of the disputed trademarks belonged to the appellant. TMT Company has no right to succeed to the rights of Dongming Company. The appellant never issued any document proving that the TMT trademark belonged to the appellee. Therefore, the judgment of the first instance awarding the disputed trademarks to the appellee lacks factual basis; the judgment of the first instance applied the law incorrectly. The judgment of the first instance failed to apply any provisions of the Trademark Law or its Implementing Regulations, nor did it apply the provisions of Article 69 of the General Principles of the Civil Law concerning the protection of trademark rights. By determining that the appellee owns the trademark rights, it lacked legal basis; the matter adjudicated by the court of first instance was not within the jurisdiction of the People's Court. Further, awarding substantial state-owned assets to a Hong Kong company would cause serious loss of state assets and is contrary to national interests. The judgment of the first instance cannot stand.

The appellee, TMT Company, argued in its defense: Trademark rights are civil rights, and disputes over trademark ownership fall within the scope of civil litigation accepted by the People's Court. The TMT, TMC, and SMT trademarks were designed by Wang Shaoming, Chairman of TMT Company. Pursuant to the agreement between Dongming Company and the appellant and the branded trade contracts, Wang Shaoming delivered the trademarks to the appellant for use and entrusted it to handle the registration matters in mainland China. After Dongming Company ceased operations, Wang Shaoming established TMT Company to take over the former company's business, and succeeded to the civil rights of Dongming Company related to the three trademarks. Therefore, there is a de facto trust legal relationship between Light Industrial Products Company and TMT Company. TMT Company never accepted any entrustment from Light Industrial Products Company to handle overseas trademark registration. Given that Light Industrial Products Company breached the parties' agreement, TMT Company has the right to demand the return of its civil rights. The judgment of the first instance found the facts correctly and applied the law properly, and the appellee requests its affirmance.

Facts Found by the Court

It was found upon trial that during the spring of 1979 at the Chinese Export Commodities Fair, during the negotiations between the Light Industrial Products Company and Wang Shaoming, an intention was reached for the Hong Kong partner to provide a trademark. At that time, Wang Shaoming was the sole shareholder of Dongming Trading Company, which was not the same entity as Dongming Company, and there was no succession relationship between them. Dongming Company was established in November of the same year. The "TMT" trademark provided by Dongming Company was a combined word and design trademark designed by Wang Shaoming based on the first letters of the English name words of the original Dongming Trading Company and Dongming Company, combined with the diamond-shaped pattern from the entry stamp of Saudi Arabian Customs. "SMT" was a trademark similar to "TMT" designed based on the initial *pinyin* of "Shao Ming" (SHAO MING). Since Registered Trademark No. 142201 registered the word "TMT" but did not completely follow Wang Shaoming's designed combined pattern of word plus diamond, in April 1983, the Light Industrial Products Company, at the request of Wang Shaoming, legal representative of TMT Company (Dongming Company had ceased business), applied to the State Trademark Office for the registration of No. 200833, a combined word and design trademark for TMT. This combined trademark was completely identical to the trademark actually used on the products manufactured with designated brands on the mainland and to the trademark registered and advertised by TMT Company abroad, and is also the core trademark in dispute in this case. The Light Industrial Products Company successively registered the TMT trademark for five categories of goods, the TMC trademark for two categories of goods, and the SMT trademark for two categories of goods on the mainland, and also registered three trademarks in relevant countries. As of August 21, 1999, TMT Company had registered 78 TMT and other trademarks on the mainland, in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and in other countries and regions worldwide. To succeed to the relevant rights of Dongming Company, TMT Trading Co., Ltd. repaid debts owed by Dongming Company to the Light Industrial Products Company totalling over HKD 3.17 million on June 5, 1982, and April 15, 1983, respectively. In a document dated September 3, 1982, from the Light Industrial Products Company to the Provincial Foreign Trade Bureau (82) Yue Qing Chu Si Zi No. 1164, it was confirmed that, after deducting the debts offset by raw and auxiliary materials provided free of charge by Dongming Company, the remaining debts of HKD 3,113,667 were to be repaid privately by Wang Shaoming and Lin Guiquan. The actual amount repaid by TMT Company on behalf of Dongming Company exceeded the debt amount confirmed by the Light Industrial Products Company in the said document. The Light Industrial Products Company denied having issued two certifying documents dated October 23, 1987, and December 16, 1987, and suspected that the two documentary exhibits were forgeries. It applied to the original trial court for a judicial appraisal of the authenticity of the seals on the two documentary exhibits regarding trademark ownership submitted by TMT Company. During the second instance of this court, the Light Industrial Products Company changed its request to apply for an appraisal of the creation time and the sequence of typing and sealing of the two documents. Entrusted by this court, the Beijing Huaxia Appraisal Center for Material Evidence conducted an appraisal, concluding that both documents were prepared in the second half of 1987, with typing occurring before the affixing of the seals. To verify the authenticity of the documents, TMT Company also provided a certification from Li Kam Man & Co., Solicitors, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, confirming that the document dated October 23, 1987, had been used by that law firm in another case on April 19, 1988, indicating that the signing and sealing date of the document was accurate. On December 7, 1994, the Light Industrial Products Company issued a notice to TMT Company, Yue Qing Chu Ye Yang <1994> No. 262, "Notice on Strengthening the Management of the TMT Trademark," which stated: "The 'TMT' trademark is a well-known trademark created through our joint operations over many years. To cherish this intangible property, after many rounds of negotiation, both parties signed an 'Agreement' on October 6 this year to facilitate, promote, strengthen, and improve management, more effectively combat counterfeit goods, promptly stop infringements, and protect our legitimate rights and interests." The multiple exclusive agency agreements and transaction confirmations signed over the years between TMT Company and the Light Industrial Products Company (including agreements dated January 5, 1983, November 3, 1984, and January 13, 1986) and the confirmations signed between Dongming Company and the Light Industrial Products Company (dated November 27, 1979, and December 8, 1980) all clearly stated that nameplates and trademarks were provided by TMT Company or Dongming Company.

Other facts found by the original trial judgment are substantially true.

Opinion of the Court

This court holds that the trademark right is a civil property right. Although the law has special provisions regarding the acquisition, term, and transfer of trademark rights, it does not vest the authority to determine ownership in administrative organs. From the nature of the trademark right, ownership litigation is a civil action for confirmation and should fall within the scope of civil cases accepted by the People's Courts. The appellant's ground for appeal that disputes over trademark ownership do not fall within the scope of cases accepted by the People's Courts is untenable. The combined word and diamond pattern trademarks such as TMT constitute the core trademarks in dispute in this case and are consistent with the trademarks used on exported goods and the trademarks promoted by TMT Company. These trademarks were designed by Wang Shaoming, who served as the shareholder and general manager of the original Dongming Company and is now the shareholder and legal representative of TMT Company, during his tenure as the legal representative of Dongming Trading Company and the general manager of Dongming Company. Wang Shaoming was the earliest and primary person in charge of the trade contracts between Dongming Company and the Light Industrial Products Company. Based on witness testimony and relevant agreements and contracts for manufacturing with designated brands, it can be determined that he, on behalf of Dongming Company, proposed that Dongming Company provide the trademark, and the Light Industrial Products Company would organize the production of TMT, TMC, and other brand ceiling fans according to the provided trademark. The Light Industrial Products Company agreed to this requirement. Wang Shaoming also first proposed the idea of registering the TMT and other trademarks domestically. Due to misleading by the Light Industrial Products Company, Dongming Company mistakenly believed that Hong Kong companies could not register trademarks on the mainland at that time. Therefore, it was agreed with the Light Industrial Products Company that the Light Industrial Products Company would handle the trademark registration in China. After Dongming Company ceased operations, the Light Industrial Products Company, at the request of Wang Shaoming, the legal representative of TMT Company at the time, registered the disputed trademark No. 200833, a combined word and design trademark, in China. According to the contract terms for manufacturing with designated brands, the Light Industrial Products Company was responsible for organizing the production of TMT brand ceiling fans and handling export procedures, while Dongming Company was responsible for providing nameplates and trademarks, advertising the products, contacting for orders, and exclusively selling all products to overseas countries and regions. During the performance of the contract, TMT Company took over from Dongming Company the responsibilities of providing technology, supervising production, exclusively selling products, conducting all product advertising, and assuming the obligation to repay the debts owed to the Light Industrial Products Company on behalf of Dongming Company. Wang Shaoming designed and provided the TMT and other trademarks on behalf of Dongming Company for the purpose of having the Light Industrial Products Company produce goods bearing the brands designated by Dongming Company under a manufacturing contract with designated brands. The parties had actually performed the manufacturing contract with designated brands, thus forming a *de facto* legal relationship of property trust regarding the trademark rights. Trademark No. 200833 was directly registered by the Light Industrial Products Company at the request of Wang Shaoming, acting as the legal representative of TMT Company. This legal relationship between the appellant and the appellee is not only evidenced by the design, delivery for use, and request for registration of the trademarks but also by the terms of the parties' trade contract for manufacturing with designated brands and the fact that only Dongming Company (later TMT Company) conducted product sales and advertising of the goods and trademarks, gradually establishing the reputation and asset appreciation of the disputed trademarks. The content of the two certifying documents issued by the Light Industrial Products Company on October 23, 1987, and December 16, 1987, while proving the existence of a commission relationship between the Light Industrial Products Company and TMT Company for trademark registration and management, also corroborates the existence of such a commission relationship between Dongming Company and the Light Industrial Products Company prior to Dongming Company's cessation of business. These two pieces of evidence have been verified as authentic through appraisal. Additionally, Li Kam Man & Co., Solicitors, Hong Kong, confirmed that the certifying document dated October 23, 1987, was used in 1988. Therefore, the two pieces of evidence should be admitted. The disputed trademarks in this case were registered domestically by the Light Industrial Products Company based on the commission and request of Dongming Company. The Light Industrial Products Company is the nominal owner of the relevant trademarks, while TMT Company is the substantive owner. Under circumstances where the Light Industrial Products Company requested the seizure of TMT Company's exported products, TMT Company, acting as the principal, requested the return of the TMT trademarks to it, which has ample factual basis. The original trial court's judgment ordering the return of the trademark rights to TMT Company in accordance with the relevant provisions of the General Principles of the Civil Law was correct. However, the original trial judgment found the existence of a commission relationship but failed to consider the fact that the trademarks were registered and managed in the name of the agent, thus not finding the existence of a trust relationship. This finding was inappropriate. The agreement signed by the parties in 1994 again stipulated the issue of trademark ownership. Based on TMT Company's statement and the Light Industrial Products Company's notice letter of July 1994, it can be determined that the purpose of signing this agreement was to strengthen trademark management and combat counterfeit goods. Since disputes had not yet arisen between the parties at that time, and TMT Company had not raised the issue of returning the trademark rights—the Light Industrial Products Company still being the trademark registrant—the clause regarding trademark rights in this agreement should be viewed as a confirmation of the status quo of the trademark rights at that time and does not affect TMT Company's claim for return of the trademark rights after disputes arose. Because the Light Industrial Products Company applied for and obtained intellectual property customs protection measures, causing TMT Company to be unable to export goods for nearly two years and suffering huge losses, the Light Industrial Products Company should be liable for this. Given that TMT Company did not appeal the dismissal of its claim for compensation, this court upholds that part of the judgment. The sales market for TMT brand products is outside China. TMT Company has registered the TMT and other trademarks in major overseas markets and enjoys exclusive trademark rights. Therefore, it is difficult for the Light Industrial Products Company to use TMT and other trademarks for export goods and lacks profitability. At the same time, because TMT Company is unable to place orders for export with domestic manufacturers, domestic manufacturers have also suffered huge losses and cannot supply goods to foreign markets, leading to market contraction. Therefore, the Light Industrial Products Company's argument that the court should protect its trademark rights on the ground of preventing loss of State-owned assets is not persuasive and lacks factual basis. During the second instance of this court, TMT Company agreed to increase the amount of compensation, which this court approves. In summary, the appellant's appeal lacks factual and legal basis and should not be upheld. The original trial judgment had clear facts and correctly applied the law. Except for the compensation amount being too low and unfair, which should be modified, the other aspects of the judgment were correct and should be affirmed. The original trial judgment had some inappropriate wording in stating the reasons for the judgment and the main text, which should be amended. Pursuant to Article 4 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 153(1)(1) and 153(1)(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court renders the following judgment:

1.  Affirm item 4 of the Civil Judgment (1998) Yue Fa Zhi Chu Zi No. 2 of the Guangdong High People's Court.

2.  Amend items 1 and 2 of the Civil Judgment (1998) Yue Fa Zhi Chu Zi No. 2 of the Guangdong High People's Court as follows: The exclusive right to use the TMT, TMC, and SMT word trademarks and the combined word and design trademarks registered in China by Guangdong Provincial Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Company shall belong to TMT Trading Co., Ltd. Guangdong Provincial Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Company shall assist TMT Trading Co., Ltd. in completing the procedures for changing the trademark registrant within one month from the effective date of this judgment.

3.  Amend item 3 of the Civil Judgment (1998) Yue Fa Zhi Chu Zi No. 2 of the Guangdong High People's Court as follows: TMT Trading Co., Ltd. shall pay compensation of RMB 2,500,000 to Guangdong Provincial Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Company, to be paid within one month from the effective date of this judgment.

The case acceptance fee for the first instance is RMB 510,000, of which RMB 255,000 shall be borne by TMT Trading Co., Ltd. and RMB 255,000 by Guangdong Provincial Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Company. The case acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 510,000, of which RMB 255,000 shall be borne by TMT Trading Co., Ltd. and RMB 255,000 by Guangdong Provincial Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Company. The appraisal fee of RMB 50,000 shall be borne by Guangdong Provincial Light Industrial Products Import and Export (Group) Company.

This judgment is final.
